title: Planning Over Rough Ground: Paying for Sand and Slope in Energy, Paying for Risk, and When the Shortest Way Is Not the Cheapest

questions.question: What does the work per metre over a cell depend on, besides the surface?
options: The cell's distance from the goal
The slope along the heading the vehicle takes
questions.explanation: The work is the weight times the rolling resistance plus the sine of the slope along the direction of travel. Going up a slope costs far more than going across it.

questions.question: A metre up a slope of 14 degrees cost, against across it:
questions.explanation: Across the slope only rolling resistance is paid. Up it, the weight times the sine of 14 degrees is added for every metre.

questions.question: The shortest path across the sand band cost, and the cheapest:
options: 90 J and 66 J, at 16.0 m and 31.2 m
questions.explanation: Straight through the sand was 16.0 m and 90 J. Round by the gravel ford was nearly twice as far and cost 66 J.

questions.question: Crossing the patch of risk, the worst cell cost was:
options: 0 with no weight and 200 with one
200 with no weight and 0 with one
questions.explanation: With no weight on risk the patch is as good as any ground, so the shortest path crosses it. With a weight the planner went round.

questions.question: Why does the planner price a step and not a cell?
options: A step is cheaper to compute
The cost depends on the heading, on a slope
questions.explanation: The same cell is cheap to cross along the contour and dear to climb, so the price belongs to the move from one cell to the next.

questions.question: What does a goal in a ring of blocked cells give?
options: found = false and an empty path, after 6476 expansions
A path that crosses the ring at its thinnest
A path to the ring's edge
questions.explanation: A step into a blocked cell is never allowed, so no path exists. The planner says so after exhausting what it can reach.
